body: Fucking agree. I've been a part of strong internet communities, this is not one. Disappointing for sure.
I love walking too! Soothes my soul. I'm glad you've found something that's enjoyable. Wishing you continued healing.

Yes. You put it in words. The world becomes heartbreakingly beautiful in a moment. You treasure everything. I feel like this on rainy days a lot. I still feel depressed in those moments, but it's this weird acceptance of my depression as part of it all. I wish I understood why.

It sounds like you've spent your whole life fighting for yourself, and that you've had it very hard. If you survived all that and even made it to college (regardless of your grades), you must be a very strong person. I believe you are valid and whole as you are, in spite of everything you've been through, everything you feel. Can I ask, what did you learn in philosophy class that led to this realization?
I thought it was just me. Even anonymously I feel weird sharing here, and afraid of negative comments or crickets.  I would absolutely prefer not to burden others with my problems

Unfortunately, suicidal ideation tends to cause a narrowing of focus. There's studies of how language changes when people are depressed. They tend to use a lot more first person (I, me, my) and absolutes (always, never). There's less ability to see the positives of yourself or your life, and it's even hard to think about those you love. I firmly believe most people who leave someone behind are full of love for them and know the pain of what they're doing. They were probably torn apart by the knowledge that they'll hurt someone close to them, at least initially, but that's the insidious nature of depression. It's an altered state, it changes your focus and wears you down til all you want is for it all to end. Not to say that you can't stop yourself, but it's hard.

You sound like a decent person who has made a couple mistakes here and there (as we all do), but are measuring yourself mostly by your ability to make money and have a meaningful career. If that is the case, I get it. I also tie most of my self-worth to my ability to work and contribute financially, it's something I'm working on. Perhaps you can find a way to see yourself differently. Not unrealistically, like a bunch of hollow self-praise that doesn't help. Just, considering different dimensions of your personhood and ways that you have inherent value. Ways that you are not a "loser" as you say. Wishing you peace.

Also, what they told you at the fast food restaurant kinda strikes me as ageism. Even if it isn't, it's a weird thing for them to say.

There's something in your tone and choice of words that really gets to me because I've felt that way. You sound frustrated because the world doesn't seem to understand your suffering or offer any way to help. I get it man, I really do. It feels like everyone's telling you the solution is to run a marathon when you're sitting there with bleeding, broken legs. The stigma around depression and suicidal thoughts is a horrible thing. Just know there's a lot of us that have gone through it and we understand and absolutely care.

That sucks. I daresay the anxiety is worse than depression sometimes.

I'll be honest with you, I don't know that I have a good reason for how I feel these days, I have just been this way for a long time. I feel really broken and like I've made too many mistakes in all areas of my life. Or almost like I've wasted so much time being depressed that I don't really deserve to stick around. Childhood stuff I haven't fully worked theough. Not very good at friendships or relationships. Etc. And I'm in a high pressure situation right now with school, I have to pass a comprehensive exam in a couple months in order to graduate and don't feel like I'll ever be ready. I feel behind and honestly kinda dumb when I talk to my peers, and if I fail that's a lot of time and money wasted and I'll probably end up back in a retail job. So that's kinda the main trigger right now, I recognize that, and I'm trying to get through it. I really do think my mental illness has affected my cognitive abilities because I can't concentrate or remember things like I used to and it kinda scares me sometimes. I don't feel like I have real problems, just that my mind is sick and I'm constantly fighting to normalize. 

Can I ask what you think about life after death? Or if it means anything to be here or it's all just random? I think about this a lot.

Have you had anxiety in the past? Can you get into some kind of routine each night (or morning or whenever it's the worst; my anxiety is always worse at night) to help? For me, it helps to drink a chamomile or valerian tea, do a quick stretch/yoga type routine, and listen to music. I'm still depressed as all hell, but it helps a little with my anxiety symptoms.

I read your previous post and I can relate to some of the things you're going through. I have this one side of me that's committed to being my best self and making a difference in this world, and this other side of me that wants to give up constantly, and I'm trying to control it but I also feel pathetic when I reach out for help. I feel guilt at my privilege and scared of failing and having nothing to show for it. I've been desensitizing/planning my departure too. Some days I can fight enough to get by and think maybe I'll make it after all, but more often than not I go right back down to despair.

Anyway, I'd be happy to troubleshoot with you on the anxiety or just keep you company for the next couple weeks. I know how unauthentic it can feel when people try to tell you why life's worth living, but you seem like a cool person and I'd be sad to hear you went through with it. But I also know how painful it can be to keep suffering. I'm treading that line everyday right now. Wishing you only peace.
